sources.entry: A list of postmortems on Github

summary.one_liner: A curated, categorized list of public incident post-mortems from companies and projects such as Amazon, Google, Cloudflare, GitHub and CircleCI, each with a short description of the failure.
summary.what_it_does: This is an awesome-style link collection rather than software. The README is organized into categories: Config Errors, Hardware/Power Failures, Conflicts, Time, Database, Uncategorized, Other lists of postmortems, Analysis and Contributors. Each entry names the company or project, gives a one-to-few-sentence summary of what went wrong, and sometimes lists the remediation or impact. Many entries are paraphrased write-ups of incidents with dates, durations and root causes, such as DNS, BGP, leap-second, and database failover incidents. The list also points to other collections of postmortems and to analysis pieces. The README shown is truncated, so later sections were not fully visible.
use_cases: Studying how large cloud and internet services failed in production
Finding real-world examples of outages for incident review training
Learning common failure patterns such as bad configs, DNS, and database failovers
Preparing blameless postmortem write-ups by comparing past examples
Researching outage history for a specific provider like AWS, Google Cloud or Cloudflare
notable: Organized by failure type: config errors, hardware/power, conflicts, time, database
Covers many well-known providers, including AWS, Google, Cloudflare, GitHub and Knight Capital
Includes a section linking to other lists of postmortems and analysis articles
Entries summarize root causes and remediations in short prose
caveats: Entries are brief summaries; the full postmortems live at external links
The list is manually curated and may not be complete or up to date
Source README is truncated in the provided text, so later sections were not reviewed
